name: B747
mesh_airframe: Boeing 747-400 (FlightGear model by Gijs de Rooy et al.)

gear_geometry.source: every object in 747-400_gear.ac is landing gear (nlg_*, blg_*, wlg_*, nosewheel.NNN are the nose, body and wing gear trucks and their wheels; the modeller named the main-truck wheels 'nosewheel'); the gear doors and wells are in 747-400_fuselage.ac (nlg_*_door) and are not gear contact geometry. Measured 2026-09-25 from the pinned commit: lowest gear vertex -5.625 m below the model origin (the nose wheels), main-truck wheels -4.79 m

dimensions_m.source: Boeing 747-400 Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning, D6-58326-1, section 2.2 (overall length 70.66 m, tail height 19.41 m); span is taken from the flown FDM's own <wingspan>

nose.source: the FDM's structural origin taken as the nose tip: its NOSE_LG contact sits 10.06 m aft of the origin, matching the type's nose-gear station (D6-58326-1, section 2.2); z at the CG waterline

tail.source: nose tip + the type's overall length 70.66 m (D6-58326-1, section 2.2) at the CG waterline

category.source: FAA TCDS A20WE (Boeing 747-400), certification basis 14 CFR Part 25 -- unverified here: from memory of the TCDS

n_z_pos_g.source: 14 CFR 25.337(b): positive limit manoeuvring load factor n = 2.1 + 24000/(W+10000), not less than 2.5; 2.5 at the 747-400's weights

n_z_neg_g.source: 14 CFR 25.337(c): negative limit manoeuvring load factor not less than -1.0 up to V_C

speed_limit_kt.source: unverified here: from memory of the 747-400 Airplane Flight Manual limitations (V_MO 365 KIAS); compared here against JSBSim calibrated airspeed without a position-error correction

m_mo.source: unverified here: from memory of the 747-400 Airplane Flight Manual limitations (M_MO 0.92)

alpha_stall_deg.reason: the JSBSim B747 model states no alpha limit (no <alphalimits> element; grep of B747.xml, 2026-09-28)

limits.note: The JSBSim B747 model is a generic 747; the placard values are the -400's. Measured 2026-09-28: the model trims and flies at 385 kt CAS at 1500 m (V_MO + 20) and at Mach 0.89 at 11000 m, so both speed limits are reachable on this model.

loading.source: JSBSim 1.2.4 aircraft/B747/B747.xml <mass_balance> and <propulsion> as shipped in the .venv wheel (read 2026-09-28); the maximum weight from memory of the 747-400 type data [unverified here]

datum.xml: the B747.xml <location> x in inches, positive aft (the JSBSim structural frame); the XML names no reference point
datum.poh: the AFM balance envelope is stated in percent MAC against a datum the XML does not name [unverified here]

arm_comparison.reason: no handbook arm is transcribed and the envelope is in percent MAC of an unnamed datum: the XML CG cannot be placed on the handbook chart, so the envelope check is refused by name (loading.datum_unverified) and the loading is flown at the XML's own arms
